main.t: A small rectangular bone at the front of the inner wall of the orbit (lacrimal bone).

simpler.t: The lacrimal bone is a tiny bone at the inner corner of your eye socket.

deeper.t: Tears drain from the eye through a canal beside it into the nose.

facts.t: It forms the front part of the medial wall of the orbit.
With the ethmoid bone, it makes up much of the medial wall.
It is paired: one in each orbit.

simpler.t: It sits at the inner corner of each eye socket.

deeper.t: Its canal opens into the nasal cavity, behind the inferior nasal concha.

items.name: Shape
items.t: A small, rectangular plate of bone.

items.name: Lacrimal fossa
items.t: A shallow hollow in its front part.

items.name: Nasolacrimal canal
items.t: Runs down from the fossa towards the nasal cavity.

items.name: Orbital surface
items.t: Forms the front of the medial wall of the orbit.

simpler.t: It is a tiny plate of bone with a hollow and a canal for tears.

deeper.t: Tears drain into the canal at the inner (medial) corner of the eye.

facts.t: Tears keep the surface of the eye moist, then drain at the inner corner into its canal.
The duct carries them down into the nasal cavity.
With a flood of tears, some fluid drains forwards in the nose, causing a runny nose.

simpler.t: It holds the start of the drain that takes tears from your eye into your nose.

items.name: Ethmoid bone
items.t: Behind it; together they form much of the medial wall of the orbit.

items.name: Nasolacrimal duct
items.t: Carries tears from the eye down into the nasal cavity.

items.name: Inferior nasal concha
items.t: The duct opens into the nasal cavity behind it.

items.name: Orbit
items.t: Forms the front of its medial wall.

simpler.t: It sits beside the ethmoid bone in the eye socket, at the top of the tear drain.

facts.t: Like the other flat bones of the face, it forms directly from membrane (intramembranous ossification).
facts.check: OpenStax 6.4 says the flat bones of the face form from membrane, but 7.5 says the facial bones form from cartilage; which applies to the lacrimal bone needs an approved source.

facts.t: The flat bones of the face are the last to ossify from membrane. They reach adult size at the end of the adolescent growth spurt.

items.injury: Crying, or an irritated eye, increases the flow of tears.
items.damaged: Nothing is damaged: the tear drain is working, but overloaded.
items.cannotDo: Keep the nose dry: tears run forwards out of the nose.
items.why: Tears normally drain backwards in the nasal cavity; extra fluid also drains forwards.

items.injury: A baby’s tear duct has not fully opened.
items.cannotDo: Drain tears: the eye waters all the time.
items.why: Tears can leave the eye only through this duct into the nose.
items.check: A blocked tear duct in babies is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20); the duct’s course is.

items.q: Explain why crying gives you a runny nose.
model: Tears drain at the inner corner of the eye into the nasolacrimal canal.
The duct opens into the nasal cavity, behind the inferior nasal concha.
With many tears, some also drains forwards and out of the nose.

items.q: Compare the lacrimal and ethmoid bones in the medial wall of the orbit.
model: Both form much of the medial wall.
The lacrimal bone is small and lies in front.
The ethmoid lies behind it, between the orbit and the nasal cavity.
The ethmoid contains air cells; the lacrimal bone holds the tear canal.

items.q: Predict where eye drops go after you blink.
model: They drain at the inner corner of the eye.
They pass into the nasolacrimal canal, beside the lacrimal bone.
The duct carries them down into the nasal cavity.
They drain backwards in the nose.

check.stem: Where does the nasolacrimal duct open?
check.why: It opens into the nasal cavity, behind the inferior nasal concha.

check.stem: Which part of the orbit does the lacrimal bone form?
options: The front of the medial wall
check.why: It forms the anterior, medial wall of the orbit.

check.stem: Why does crying give you a runny nose?
options: Extra tears drain forwards in the nasal cavity
check.why: With increased tears, some fluid drains anteriorly in the nasal cavity.
